description: Passive joint moments, one row per joint. A measured row gives, for each direction away from neutral, the onset angle (rad) and polynomial stiffness [k0 Nm/rad, k1 Nm/rad^2, k2 Nm/rad^3] of the restoring moment M = -(k0 x + k1 x^2 + k2 x^3) sign-adjusted per side, with x the displacement beyond the onset. Gap rows list where values could come from; no value is used without a verified source. The measured rows are neutral-centred linear stiffness (onset 0): they act over the whole joint range, not only at its end, and are validated only inside valid_range. They do not by themselves model end-range stiffening, so they will not stop a controller from resting on a hard joint limit; an end-range row needs its own source or an explicit, documented extrapolation. Every applied row has a source_curve; its springs are fitted to the residual (source curve minus the model's own passive muscle moment at act = 0, at the source's posture; only its restoring part), per side of the residual's equilibrium by non-negative least squares over fit.range_rad (scripts/fit_passive_moments.py); onsets are absolute joint angles. Every row is scales_with 'none' (measured stiffness is kept unless a subject measurement exists); scales_with is provenance metadata for later subject scaling. The model itself is the generated block of myoarm_r_tendon.xml written from this table by scripts/fit_passive_moments.py; every measured and assumed row is applied (the status is provenance). A row with a damping entry sets that joint's damping (N m s/rad), written by the same script into myoarm_r_chain.xml; the other joints keep their class damping.

joints.notes: Not added. MyoHand's forearm muscles already supply most of Formica's value through their passive force-length curves, and that contribution depends on posture: 0.22 Nm/rad about pro_sup = 0 in a two-arm MyoHand model at elbow 90 deg (act = ctrl = 0), 0.056 Nm/rad in myoarm_r / myofullbody (myo_personalise measurement). Adding Formica on top would double-count; a pose-independent subtraction would be wrong. Revisit with an end-range source.

The abduction term c*exp(d(theta - theta_max)) is left out: with the averaged coefficients (c = -2.94 +- 8.2, d = -0.18) it gives about -11 N m at the resting adduction, against at most -1.9 N m measured, so the averaged pair is not usable. Flexion beyond rest was not measured, so the row only resists extension. MyoHand's muscles give <= 2.1 N cm passive moment here (at 30-40 deg extension), against up to 150 N cm in the source: no double counting worth subtracting. These muscle figures predate the thenar muscles: with AdP, FPB and APB the model's passive CMC moment reaches about 0.6 N m near the limits, so the springs are fitted to the residual (subtract_model_muscles).
joints.where: Table 1 means (n=10), Eq. (2) first term; Sec. 3.1 ranges

source_curve.mapping: Domalain's Mp is the external moment (negative = extension) in Chao et al. TMC coordinates with angles relative to each subject's maxima; the internal moment is -Mp. phi_max (maximal extension, -43.2 +- 16.0 deg) is aligned with MyoHand's cmc_flexion extension limit (+0.70 rad; +q = extension), as the paper prescribes relative-to-maximum use; fit over the measured range of motion (54.9 deg) from that limit.

subtract_model_muscles.note: Domalain's moment is the total passive CMC moment: the model's muscle moment (thenar muscles included) at act = 0 is subtracted.

joints.axes_note: Hollister et al. 1992: the CMC flexion-extension axis lies in the trapezium and the abduction-adduction axis in the metacarpal base, 72.7 +- 8.4 deg apart and not intersecting. MyoHand's two CMC axes are 80.9 deg apart and intersect (both on firstmc). Domalain used Chao et al. Euler angles, so the mapping is by joint limits, not by axes.

joints.notes: Barry et al. 2018 likewise used Domalain 2010 for thumb CMC abduction. The flexion term e*exp(f(phi - phi_max)) (e = -71.89, f = -0.55) is left out (single-joint springs): it is below 5 N cm unless the CMC is within ~5 deg of maximal extension. MyoHand's muscles give no passive CMC abduction moment (|M| < 0.1 N cm), so nothing double-counts. These muscle figures predate the thenar muscles: with AdP, FPB and APB the model's passive CMC moment reaches about 0.6 N m near the limits, so the springs are fitted to the residual (subtract_model_muscles).
joints.where: Table 1 means (n=10), Eq. (3) without the flexion term; Sec. 3.1 ranges

source_curve.mapping: theta_max (maximal abduction, 7.4 +- 8.5 deg) aligned with MyoHand's cmc_abduction abduction limit (+0.78 rad); fit over the measured abduction-adduction span (7.4 - (-39.9) = 47.3 deg). MyoHand's range reaches 26 deg further into adduction, where the fitted cubic is extrapolated. The adduction side is a single linear spring: a cubic fitted inside the measured span extrapolates to 5.5-6.8 N m at MyoHand's adduction limit (the source exponential to 7.3 N m), the linear one to 1.8 N m, near Domalain's largest measured moment (141.7 +- 43.9 N cm at the subjects' maximal adduction).

joints.notes: Assumption from Barry et al. 2018 (no thumb MCP data exist): the index MCP's total static torque (Kamper 2002, wrist and IP neutral) with MyoHand's thumb sign (+q = extension), minus the thumb muscles' own passive moment (thenar on). The total, not Knutson's intrinsic part, because the thumb has no extrinsic finger tenodesis to supply the rest; Knutson's intrinsic equilibrium (57 deg) lies outside the thumb MP range (45 deg flexion) and drove the thumb into its flexion limit. Outside Kamper's operating points (-10..60 deg flexion) the torque is held at its edge values rather than extrapolated: the PIP cubic turns back toward flexion above 45.5 deg (+0.064 N m at 90 deg), the DIP cubic falls to -0.25 N m at 90 deg, and the MCP cubic reaches 0.23 N m at 40 deg hyperextension.

joints.notes: Intrinsic component only (Knutson Eq. 2, Table 1 medians of 8 healthy subjects; units N cm, 1/deg, deg; theta = MCP flexion). The extrinsic component (Eq. 3, wrist dependent) belongs to the extrinsic muscle-tendon units and is not added. Validation: MyoHand's extrinsic index muscles (FDS2, FDP2, EDC2, EIP) give at most 1.2 N cm passive MCP moment over MCP 0-90 deg and wrist -60..60 deg, against Knutson's extrinsic fit of up to 30 N cm (e.g. -30 N cm at MCP 90 deg, wrist flexed 60 deg): the model lacks the extrinsic passive tension (tenodesis), so with the intrinsic curve alone the relaxed MCP settles near its intrinsic equilibrium (~55 deg flexion) instead of ~27 deg (intrinsic + extrinsic at wrist 0). The intrinsic muscles (RI2, LU_RB2, UI_UB2) add little passive moment. RI2's path used to jump by 7 mm between MCP 10 and 15 deg (its insertion entered the 2ndmcp wrap cylinder, and the sidesite forced a dorsal wrap below that) and gave -5..-9 N cm (extension) at MCP 0-10 deg; RI2 now runs without that wrap, continuous and within its lengthrange.
